title: Life, Liberty and Dignity PIL — Article 21 (Art. 21)

content.overview: Article 21 is a principal substantive anchor for PIL: no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Expanded readings of life and dignity support public-interest claims for vulnerable classes, subject to standing, forum, and abuse filters under Articles 32 and 226.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is life, liberty, or dignity engaged? (2) Whose rights — class unable to approach? (3) Forum 32 or 226? (4) Bona fides? (5) Precise relief?
content.study:
Core rule: Article 21 supplies the rights base for many structural PILs — bonded labour, custodial conditions, basic dignity claims. PIL standing allows representative enforcement; it does not invent rights beyond Article 21 and related Part III guarantees.

Expanded life and dignity: Courts have read Article 21 to include aspects of dignified existence. In PIL, plead the concrete deprivation and the public or class character of the injury.

Forum: Article 32 for Supreme Court Part III enforcement; Article 226 for High Court, including where other legal rights join the claim.

Limits: Private disputes, vague policy wish-lists, and motivated petitions fail even when Article 21 is recited.

Current-law framing: Name Article 21 and the writ article. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Article 21 as PIL rights base
sections.body: Life and personal liberty, read with dignity, ground many public-interest petitions for classes that cannot litigate individually.

sections.heading: Representative enforcement
sections.body: Liberal standing lets a bona fide petitioner seek enforcement of Article 21 for others who face access barriers.

sections.heading: Concrete injury and relief
sections.body: Plead specific deprivations and implementable directions; avoid omnibus governance prayers without legal duty.

sections.heading: Forum under Articles 32 and 226
sections.body: Choose Supreme Court or High Court by rights base, scale, and territory.

sections.heading: Abuse filters
sections.body: Article 21 citation does not cure private rivalry or publicity petitions.

provisions.title: Protection of life and personal liberty

examples.title: Class dignity claim
examples.body: Systemic bonded labour in a region: Article 21 plus representative standing and possible continuing directions.

examples.title: Private label
examples.body: Service dispute framed only as Article 21 PIL without public class injury: abuse filter applies.

hypotheticals.question: Does every social grievance become Article 21 PIL?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. There must be a justiciable life/liberty/dignity deprivation, bona fides, and fit forum.

distinctions.title: Article 21 rights vs PIL standing
distinctions.right: Standing: who may enforce it in public interest.

misconceptions.correction: Standing, forum, concrete injury, and abuse filters still apply.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.issue: Flexible enforcement of Article 21 for vulnerable persons?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts may use flexible procedure and continuing directions for effective Fundamental Rights enforcement.
cases.holding: Petition treated as vehicle for Article 21 enforcement.
cases.relevance: Primary Article 21 PIL orientation; verification open.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.issue: When may a person approach for public injury?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed for bona fide public redress.
cases.relevance: Standing for Article 21 PILs; verification open.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.ratioDecidendi: Verify credentials, motive, public injury, absence of personal gain.
cases.relevance: Filters even for Article 21-labelled PILs; verification open.
